task.title: rle-encode
task.statement: The rle package exposes decode (already implemented) and a stub encode(s). Implement encode(s) so that it run-length encodes a string: each maximal run of one character becomes that character followed by the decimal count of the run (the count is always written, even when it is 1). For example encode('aaabbc') is 'a3b2c1', encode('abc') is 'a1b1c1', encode('') is ''. encode must return a str and must round-trip with decode (decode(encode(x)) == x for every string x). Raise TypeError when s is not a string. Do not change decode or the tests.
acceptance_criteria: TypeError when s is not a string

spec.restated_task: Implement the encode function in the rle package to perform run-length encoding on a string. Each maximal run of a single character must be represented as that character followed by its decimal count (always written, even for a count of 1). The function must return a string, raise TypeError for non-string inputs, and satisfy the round-trip property decode(encode(x)) == x for all strings x. The existing decode function must not be altered.

interface_contract.name: encode
interface_contract.behavior: Run-length encodes the input string s. Each maximal run of identical characters is replaced by the character followed by the decimal representation of the run length (always written, even for length 1). Returns the concatenated encoded string. For empty input, returns empty string.
error_cases: TypeError if s is not a string

interface_contract.name: decode
interface_contract.behavior: Decodes a run-length encoded string s. Expects each character followed by a decimal count (one or more digits). Returns the expanded string. For empty input, returns empty string.
error_cases: TypeError if s is not a string
ValueError if a character is not followed by at least one digit (missing count)

acceptance_criteria: For any string x, decode(encode(x)) == x (round-trip property). This must hold for empty string, single character, multiple runs, and runs with multi-digit counts.
encode returns a value of type str
encode raises TypeError when the input is not a string (e.g., integer, list, None)
out_of_scope: The decode function implementation and behavior must not be changed.
The test file tests/test_basic.py must not be modified.
The __init__.py files must not be modified.
The function signature of encode must remain encode(s).

sealed_tests.notes: Cover all acceptance criteria including roundtrip, error cases, and edge cases.

drift.summary: The diff implements encode exactly as specified: it validates input type, handles empty strings, produces character-count pairs for every run (including count 1), and returns a string. arbitration.headline: 1 failing test(s) indicate a real implementation bug; human review required

classifications.rationale: The contract requires the round-trip property decode(encode(x)) == x for every string x. The candidate's encode produces 'a111' for input 'a1', which decode expands to 'a' repeated 111 times, violating round-trip. This is a genuine defect in the candidate.
classifications.contract_basis: Contract: 'encode must return a str and must round-trip with decode (decode(encode(x)) == x for every string x).'

classifications.rationale: The test uses string literals '\\n\\n\\t' and '\\n2\\t1', which in Python source represent literal backslash-n sequences (six characters), not newline and tab characters. The contract does not specify this input-output pair; it only requires encode to work for any string, including actual newlines and tabs. The test is defective due to incorrect escaping.
classifications.contract_basis: Contract: 'each maximal run of one character becomes that character followed by the decimal count of the run' - the test does not faithfully encode this for newline/tab.

modules.corrected_notes: One failing test (roundtrip) reveals a genuine implementation bug: the candidate's encode does not satisfy the round-trip property for strings containing digits. The other failing test (newline/tab) is defective due to incorrect string literals in the test. Since not all failing tests are test_defects, corrected_module is null.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code; a candidate can still tamper from inside a child after the nonce was read (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED.
